rules:
M1-fine: does the coarseness of the centimetre SPEED targets explain why mixed-unit supervision
fails for speed but converts path? Written before the pool is built or anything is trained.

BACKGROUND (CPU analysis of results/courtdyn/m1_mixunit/mixunit_v3_pool.json, done before this file):
speed and path come from the same windows (431 shared windows; path/speed = 2.000, IQR 2.00-2.04),
so both families carry the same visual evidence with the same relative dispersion (CV 0.54-0.58).
The cm targets were built as the one-decimal metre answer string x 100, so every cm target is a
multiple of 10: the quantization step is 9.1% of the cm-speed median (110) but 4.7% of the cm-path
median (215), and cm-speed targets have ~1 bit less entropy (4.38 vs 5.26 bits; 34 vs 57 values).
Ruled out already on the CPU: a narrower relative spread for speed (CV equal) and test references
outside the training range (share below the training p10: speed 0.17-0.24, path 0.16-0.26).

MANIPULATION. Identical to the M1 seed-42 mixed-unit pool (same 1,120 items, images, order, the same
560 centimetre items, same metre items, same path targets, same hyperparameters as
a100/config.TRAIN_ARGS, seed 42) except that each of the 140 centimetre SPEED targets is the exact
v3 homography speed x 100 rounded to 1 cm/s (e.g. "155.0" instead of "160.0"). Adapter:
models/courtdyn-mixunit-fine-v3-s42.

TEST. Explicit prompts (m_height, cm_height) on Q2_top_480-510 and Q1_top_0-30 (the published M1
cells), speed and path. Per cell: paired cm/m ratio R, distinct centimetre answers, Spearman
rho_cm of the centimetre answers with the reference.

RULE. A speed cell CONVERTS if its centimetre arm is non-degenerate (> 2 distinct answers) AND
R >= 10 AND rho_cm >= 0.30 (the amended R2 criterion). Resolution account SUPPORTED if both speed
cells convert; NOT SUPPORTED if neither does; otherwise intermediate. Sanity: path should still
convert (R >= 10) in both cells; if it does not, the manipulation disturbed training and the verdict
is reported as confounded.

INTERPRETATION fixed now. Supported: the speed failure of mixed-unit supervision is a property of
coarse centimetre targets (a label-construction artefact), not of speed. Not supported: coarseness
is excluded, and the remaining candidate is that the adapter's own speed readings (metre medians
0.4-0.6 m/s) convert to centimetre values below the bulk of the centimetre-speed training targets
(p10 = 60), whereas its path readings convert into the bulk of the path targets -- an untested
account that the paper may state only as a hypothesis. One seed; no claim beyond seed 42.
